title: Edit a text file programmatically — file_edit
code:
tmpfile <- tempfile()  writeLines(text =              c("hello I am joe",                "this is multiple lines of text",                "12345",                "",                "^ line 4 is an empty line"),            con = tmpfile) cat(readLines(tmpfile),sep = "
") #> hello I am joe #> this is multiple lines of text #> 12345 #>  #> ^ line 4 is an empty line  # The simplest use is to append a line in a file with new text. Note that txt # must be a single character string. file_edit(file = tmpfile,           txt = "this line is appended after the second line",           match = 2,           append = TRUE) cat(readLines(tmpfile),sep = "
") #> hello I am joe #> this is multiple lines of text #> this line is appended after the second line #> 12345 #>  #> ^ line 4 is an empty line  # We can instead replace a line using append = FALSE. Here, we replace the empty # line in the file. After adding the line above, the empty line now occupies # index 5. file_edit(file = tmpfile,           txt = "this line is no longer empty",           match = 5,           append = FALSE) cat(readLines(tmpfile),sep = "
") #> hello I am joe #> this is multiple lines of text #> this line is appended after the second line #> 12345 #> this line is no longer empty #> ^ line 4 is an empty line  # The txt argument can also be a function, anonymous or named. It just needs to # accept a single string and return a single string. Here, we replace "is" with # "was" in line 6. file_edit(file = tmpfile,           txt = ~ stringr::str_replace(.x, "is", "was"),           match = 6,           append = FALSE) cat(readLines(tmpfile),sep = "
") #> hello I am joe #> this is multiple lines of text #> this line is appended after the second line #> 12345 #> this line is no longer empty #> ^ line 4 was an empty line  # The match argument can also be a  function. It just needs to accept a single # string and return a single boolean. You can use it with the txt argument # for some interesting interactions. Here, we change every line containing # the word "is" to uppercase file_edit(file = tmpfile,           txt = toupper,           match = ~ stringr::str_detect(.x, " is "),           append = FALSE) cat(readLines(tmpfile),sep = "
") #> hello I am joe #> THIS IS MULTIPLE LINES OF TEXT #> THIS LINE IS APPENDED AFTER THE SECOND LINE #> 12345 #> THIS LINE IS NO LONGER EMPTY #> ^ line 4 was an empty line  # strings containing carriage returns are preserved. Here, we use the readLines # and length functions to ensure we append the string to the end of the file multiline <- " Here is a string that takes up multiple lines"  file_edit(file = tmpfile,           txt = multiline,           match = length(readLines(tmpfile)),           append = TRUE) cat(readLines(tmpfile),sep = "
") #> hello I am joe #> THIS IS MULTIPLE LINES OF TEXT #> THIS LINE IS APPENDED AFTER THE SECOND LINE #> 12345 #> THIS LINE IS NO LONGER EMPTY #> ^ line 4 was an empty line #>  #> Here is a string #> that takes up multiple lines

title: Initialize a targets project — tar_init
text: phase_names chr vector, names target phases like "fetch", "process", etc. phase_nums int vector, numbers prepend phase_names like "1_fetch", "2_process", etc. Defaults seq_along(phase_names) home chr, root directory targets project. Defaults current working directory "." separate_phase_scripts lgl, different R script created phase like "1_fetch.R", "2_process.R", etc? FALSE, targets lists initialized _targets.R file. Defaults TRUE phase_subdirs chr vector, subdirectories within phase. Defaults "src", "" use_leading_zeros lgl, "0" used front phase numbers file directory names? overwrite lgl, initialization overwrite files folders already exist? Defaults FALSE

title: Initialize a targets project — tar_init
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # temporary directories in which targets project is initialized (you can skip # this part if creating your own project) tmp <- tempdir() unlink(tmp, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE) dir.create(tmp)  # creates 1_fetch, 2_process, 3_summarize R scripts and directories tar_init(home = tmp, phase_names = c("fetch", "process", "summarize"))  list.files(tmp, full.names = FALSE, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE,            pattern = "\\.(R|empty)$")  # clean out tmp folder unlink(tmp, recursive = TRUE, force = TRUE) dir.create(tmp)  # different structure starting with 0_config and including "in/" dir in each phase tar_init(home = tmp,          phase_names = c("config", "pull", "munge", "visualize"),          phase_nums = 0:3,          phase_subdirs = c("in", "src", "out"),          separate_phase_scripts = FALSE)  list.files(tmp, full.names = FALSE, recursive = TRUE, all.files = TRUE,            pattern = "\\.(R|empty)$") } # }

title: Set up a USGS project directory — use_project_usgs
text: home chr, root directory project. Defaults current working directory. gitignore_additions chr vector, files/directories added .gitignore NULL (default) additions. readme_type chr, either "md" create README markdown file (README.md; default) "rmd" create R markdown file (README.Rmd). Using Rmd file allow include R code output README.md. disclaimer_type chr, either "provisional" (default) include provisional software disclaimer statement "approved" approved disclaimer statement. important include approved disclaimer statement software approved software release. repo_url chr, URL Git repository. NULL (default) generic URL provided link repository CONTRIBUTING.md. Otherwise, issue page repo_url used link. use_mr_template lgl, GitLab Merge Request template included project repository. Default TRUE. open lgl; whether open files interactive editing.
